summary: PRIMARY (cold-boot white flash fix) — VERIFIED FIXED. Signed in as e2e_test_1786703401@example.com with Demo mode ON, routed to /dashboard, then instrumented an 8ms polling sampler via page.add_init_script BEFORE calling page.reload() so the sampler captures the FULL cold-boot from t=0 to t=3500ms. For every sample the probe called document.elementFromPoint at x=195, y in {100,400,700} and walked up to find the first opaque-background ancestor — this is exactly what the user visually sees at those pixels. Result across 407 samples: 0 (zero) frames where a full-screen (>=50% viewport) element painted WHITE (#FFFFFF, rgb(255,255,255)); the warm off-white (#FAF8F5, rgb(250,248,245)) was visible at all 3 probe points from t=576ms onward (352 warm-color frames captured), and dashboard-greeting first appeared at t=760ms. From t=0-440ms elementFromPoint returned null (page bytes not yet parsed/painted — this is the browser blank state BEFORE any React Native Web root paints, not a flash from within the app), then the warm background paints directly with NO intervening white frame. This confirms the three-part fix: (1) app/index.tsx boot-loading uses colors.surfaceSecondary, (2) (tabs)/_layout.tsx not-ready branch returns full-screen warm View instead of null, (3) root Stack contentStyle sets colors.surfaceSecondary so inter-screen transitions never paint white. DASHBOARD content verified: dashboard-greeting, trust-banner, lower-bills-cta (green Add-a-site-or-business banner), lower-bills-cta-pill, quick-action-scan, talk-to-human (Have a query pill) all render. REGRESSION verified: (a) all 5 tabs (Home/Sites/Reports/Support/Profile) navigate cleanly with no red screens; (b) tapping site-card-p3 in Sites opens /sites/p3 with stable site-detail-header showing 'Bristol Retail Unit', bottom app-tab-bar persists; (c) font check on 246 leaf text nodes finds 0 non-Geist non-icon fonts — no per-tab font flash regression. No deprecated Expo packages detected in the reference files.
critical_code_review_comments: app/index.tsx (line 41) correctly uses colors.surfaceSecondary as the boot-loading container background. Good.

app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx (line 21) correctly returns <View style={{flex:1, backgroundColor: colors.surfaceSecondary}} /> instead of null when !ready. This eliminates the null-render frame that previously fell through to the parent's background. Good.

app/_layout.tsx (line 61) correctly sets Stack screenOptions.contentStyle.backgroundColor = colors.surfaceSecondary so ALL screens (including intermediate route transitions) inherit the warm background at the navigator level, not just at the screen level. This is the belt-and-braces fix.

Note: app/_layout.tsx still returns `null` at line 50 when !ready (icon/app fonts not yet loaded). This is fine because SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync/hideAsync gates the native splash over that null-render window — the user never sees the null, they see the native splash. If SplashScreen ever fails to gate (e.g. web preview quirk where the native splash is a static image handoff), the null could show as browser-default background. On web that browser-default is transparent → shows the html background, which is not explicitly set anywhere. Consider adding `body { background-color: #FAF8F5; }` to any web-only CSS entry (or in app.json web config) as an additional defense. Not required today but robust hardening.
theme.ts colors.surface (#FFFFFF, cards) vs colors.surfaceSecondary (#FAF8F5, app background) are distinct and the boot fix correctly uses surfaceSecondary — no confusion between the two.
seed_data_creation: None — Demo mode uses in-app mocked GET /properties, /businesses, /renewals/urgent, /reports/spend responses.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To repro cold-boot background sampling: (1) login and persist auth (skip if already), (2) go to /dashboard once so router lands there on reload, (3) call page.add_init_script with an 8ms setInterval that stores samples in window.__bgSamples. The sampler MUST use document.elementFromPoint(x,y) + walk-up-for-first-opaque-ancestor — do NOT sample document.body/documentElement backgroundColor (React Native Web leaves those transparent). Also do NOT sample by 'biggest element with non-transparent bg' — that finds sub-cards. (4) page.reload(wait_until='commit'), (5) wait 3600ms, (6) read window.__bgSamples. Classify a WHITE flash as: any sample where any probe's opaque-ancestor has bg=='rgb(255, 255, 255)' AND the ancestor's rect area >= 50% viewport. On this fix that count is 0. Demo mode: profile-demo-toggle root uses a custom (non-aria) React Native switch (no role='switch' child with aria-checked in this build); clicking the root [data-testid='profile-demo-toggle'] element toggles it. Auth persists in localStorage across reloads within same browser context.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: cold-boot showed a visible white flash + background-colour shift before the dashboard settled. Root causes reported by main agent: (1) index.tsx boot-loading container used colors.surface (#FFFFFF, white) → white full-screen for however long AsyncStorage flags + auth-context were resolving; (2) (tabs)/_layout.tsx not-ready branch returned null → parent navigator painted whatever was underneath; (3) Root Stack had no contentStyle background → between-screen transitions could momentarily expose the html/body which is transparent → browser-default white. Fix applied by main agent flips all three to colors.surfaceSecondary (#FAF8F5). This test's 8ms-cadence probe across 407 samples during a real cold-boot confirms zero full-screen white frames between the browser's initial blank paint (t=0-440ms, pre-React-mount) and the warm dashboard (from t=576ms). No mitigation needed — fix is complete.
